title: debug_ingest.py's verdict line misstates what it judged: a fixed /12 denominator and a vacuous replay-clean pass
claim: tools/replay/debug_ingest.py prints stages_ok=12/12 when 11 checks ran, 10/12 when 8 of 10 checks passed (stores emptied), and passes replay-clean with smoke_verdict=pass on a bundle whose replay half is empty.
mechanism: main() prints 12 - len(fails) over a constant 12 while ingest() runs accuracy-loaded XOR corruption-refused and skips both when no accuracy store exists; replay-clean is not(export.violations({})) and carries no item count, so D15.md M3's 'a check passing on an empty section is vacuous' is left to the reader.

evidence.value: checks_ok=11/11 vs tool_stages_ok=12/12 (both bundles); --empty stores: checks_ok=8/10 vs tool_stages_ok=10/12; --empty replay: vacuous_passes=1 with all checks ok
evidence.machine: macOS arm64, box B8 (shared), CI venv python3

perturbation.change: --empty replay (the replay half emptied, as a download from an install without the recorder carries it)

null_control.note: the overstatement of the denominator persists (12 vs 11) even here

metric_definition: Per bundle: checks ingest() ran and passed, against the stages_ok line main() prints; passes whose section read holds 0 items.
phenomenon_property: debug_ingest.py's verdict counts the checks it ran and names a pass on an empty section as not judged.
seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D15/s1/ingest_checks.py --bundle B --empty replay|cycle_rows|stores (each check with section_items=0 and value 1 is a seam)
proposed_fix_scope: main() prints passed/ran from Results (count checks, not fails); replay-clean reports the replay row count and reads 'skipped: replay half empty (manifest.replay names why)' when it is 0; gate_checks gains the empty-replay arm.
reproduction_steps: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/replay/debug_ingest.py --bundle S (11 ok lines, stages_ok=12/12)
